host_fixture_compile.scope: Initial host test declared integer literals as i32 while casting references to u8 pointers. Fixed fixture types; no production Rust defect.

review.result: One bounded read-only Astra review found no actionable bug within BSP/AP-parked scope. Deadline publication precedes park under IF0; timer polling precedes kernel-frame early return; existing custody retains pending wake and last-attached owner. Reviewer ran no tests/build.
review.delta: Timer expiry uses wake_owned_thread after its atomic take_due claim instead of generic cancellation, avoiding cancellation of a later deadline arm. Real BOOT registration was initially placed in an unused helper; actual native checker rejected it and the final actual init path seals all18 main tasks before scheduling.
review.limits: Source review/host helpers are not physical stack, NIC IRQ, SMP or wall-clock proof. Latest normal traces establish actual timer→user return and useful peer/desktop progress; no new last-runnable hardware proof is claimed.

limits: Own existing main task only, registered by the actual BOOT RegistryBuild path. Inventory fixed32/sealed with18 current tasks, including dormant successors; signal trampolines cannot request this wait.
Kernel mechanism bounds1..64 nominal ticks and rejects overflow, existing arm and all spare arguments. Seven real Ring3 invalid-argument probes fail before park.

IPC/reply wake cancels pending timeout and retains the existing coalesced wake. Timer claim retires its own deadline and uses existing atomic task admission. Exited/fault-blocked identities cannot gain execution authority.
Timer callback scans at most32 immutable pointers without domain-registry lookup, allocation, frame edits or capability creation. It runs for kernel and user timer frames.
SexNet retains one cooperative try-listen yield, then waits two nominal ticks on empty inbox while device work is active. Ingress remains timer-assisted polling, not NIC IRQ or low-power proof.
Predictable transport seed, static IPv4, one diagnostic flow and offline app APIs persist. DNS/HTTP/TLS, firmware DMA drain/IOMMU, epoch replay, SMP/hotplug and named physical hardware remain open.
